deployments.bridge_version: Third-party LayerZero endpoint v2 OFT bridge: Avalanche PepeOFT ↔ Ethereum PepeOFTAdapter
deployments.note: Exact original Avalanche PepeOFT is its own ERC-20 token (token()=self). Pinned chain-identity-checked peers(30101) returns Ethereum adapter0x5a026ea79cda77007a474d7e5b66a663721f7979; that adapter's peers(30106) reciprocally returns the Avalanche token, and token() returns issuer-authenticated Ethereum PEPE0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933. Verified source confirms LayerZero OFT and OFTAdapter implementations and immutable canonical token/endpoint constructor arguments. Official LayerZero documentation defines these trusted peer channels and adapter locking/unlocking semantics. This version is separate from the Arbitrum/BNB endpoint v1 OFT; issuer endorsement of the bridge is not asserted. The wrapper origin and reciprocal bridge relation are proven, but official issuer/bridge-operator attribution remains unresolved. The user explicitly requested removal of this deployment from the catalog; these readings remain as research history.

deployments.bridge_version: Canonical zkSync NativeTokenVault registered Ethereum wrapper for Era-origin ZK (existing deployment)
deployments.note: Pinned Ethereum on-chain reads at block0x18e9899 prove original wrapper0x66a5… originToken()=issuer Era0x5a7d…, nativeTokenVault()=official mainnet0xbed1eb542f9a5aa6419ff3deb921a372681111f6, and assetId()=0x83e2fbc0a739b3c765de4c2b4bf8072a71ea8fbb09c8cf579c71425d8bc8804a. The official Vault reciprocally maps that asset to originChainId324 and tokenAddress0x66a5…, and assetId(wrapper) agrees. Official pinned NativeTokenVault source defines stored originChainId/tokenAddress/assetId mappings and legacy asset registration; registered current deployment is authoritative. The current factory calculation returning a different deterministic address is not evidence that this registered existing wrapper is incorrect. Source and raw readings retained in zksync-zk-bridge.json.
